questions.question: Explain how the Nuremberg Laws affected the lives of German Jews. (4 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: The Nuremberg Laws (September 1935) stripped Jews of German citizenship, reducing them to "state subjects" with no political rights. They banned marriages and sexual relationships between Jews and Germans, and forbade Jewish households from employing German women under 45. The laws made anti-Semitism official state policy, moving persecution from SA violence to systematic legal discrimination.

questions.question: Why was Kristallnacht a significant turning point? (8 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: Kristallnacht (9-10 November 1938) was a turning point because it marked the shift from legal discrimination to open, organised violence. 191 synagogues were burned, over 7,000 Jewish businesses destroyed, 91 Jews killed, and 20,000-30,000 men sent to concentration camps. questions.question: "The persecution of the Jews escalated gradually between 1933 and 1945." How far do you agree? (12 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: The persecution did escalate gradually, following a clear pattern: boycotts (1933) → legal discrimination (Nuremberg Laws 1935) → violent pogroms (Kristallnacht 1938) → ghettos (1939-1941) → mass shootings (Einsatzgruppen 1941) → extermination camps (1942-1945). questions.question: Explain the purpose and decisions of the Wannsee Conference. (8 marks)
questions.correctAnswer: The Wannsee Conference (20 January 1942) was called by Reinhard Heydrich to coordinate the "Final Solution to the Jewish Question." The 15 officials present agreed that all 11 million European Jews would be transported to extermination camps in Poland. Eichmann would organise transport logistics.
